# Web

22 endpoints (11 GET, 7 POST, 1 PATCH, 3 DELETE). Base URL `https://www.socialcrawl.dev`, auth header `x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY`.

**Credit costs:** 13 free (0 credits), 9 custom (flat/metered) - the exact cost is in each endpoint heading below.

Web endpoints scrape, search, crawl, and map arbitrary web pages, the general-purpose surface for any URL that isn't a first-class social/commerce platform. Crawl/map jobs fan out across a site and can run longer than a single-page fetch.

## POST /v1/web/agent - 25 credits (custom)

Runs a model-neutral browser agent task and returns a SocialCrawl async job id (job_...). Poll it via GET /v1/web/jobs/{job_id}.

**Use when** tasks need clicking and navigating to reach the data; for a page you can already name, scrape it.
**Cost** not cached
**Execution** Async job: pass `webhook_url` to be told when it completes instead of polling.
**Paging** none

**Body params** (JSON)

- `url` (required) - Starting URL folded into the agent instruction. · e.g. `https://example.com`
- `prompt` (required) - Task instruction. · e.g. `Find the pricing page.`
- `model` (optional, enum: spark-1-mini | spark-1-pro) - Agent model: spark-1-mini or spark-1-pro. · e.g. `spark-1-mini`

**Response** `WebPage` async job: this call returns `job_id`; poll `GET /v1/web/jobs/{job_id}` for status, and the result comes back there once it completes. Job envelope (inferred from a sample): {job_id string, kind string, resource string, status string, progress null, invalid_urls null, result_ref null, result null, error null, credits_hold number, credits_charged number, created_at string, updated_at string, expires_at string}.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/agent" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com","prompt":"Find the pricing page."}'
```

## POST /v1/web/batch-scrape - N credits for N submitted URLs (request-shaped)

Starts an async batch scrape job for multiple URLs and returns a SocialCrawl job id (job_...). Poll or cancel it via GET/DELETE /v1/web/jobs/{job_id}.

**Use when** you already know every URL you want; use crawl instead when the site should be explored for you.
**Cost** not cached
**Pricing** 1 credit per URL submitted, held up front and refunded down to the URLs actually scraped when the job settles.
**Execution** Async job: pass `webhook_url` to be told when it completes instead of polling.
**Paging** none

**Body params** (JSON)

- `urls` (required) - Array or comma-separated list of public URLs to scrape. · e.g. `https://example.com/a,https://example.com/b`
- `ignore_invalid_urls` (optional, boolean) - Skip invalid URLs instead of failing the job.
- `formats` (optional, string) - CSV of output formats for each URL, e.g. 'markdown' (default) or 'markdown,html'.
- `only_main_content` (optional, boolean) - Strip nav, headers, footers and sidebars on every URL and keep the article body. Default true.
- `proxy` (optional, enum: basic | auto | enhanced) - Proxy tier applied to every URL: basic, auto, or enhanced.
- `webhook_url` (optional, string) - HTTPS URL that receives a signed callback when the job reaches a terminal state, so you do not have to poll GET /v1/web/jobs/{job_id}.

**Response** `Analytics` async job: this call returns `job_id`; poll `GET /v1/web/jobs/{job_id}` for status, and the result comes back there once it completes ([full schema](schemas/Analytics.md)).

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `page.url` | Requested URL. |
| `page.extraction` | Structured extraction result when requested. |
| `page.fetched_at` | Fetch timestamp when reported. |
| `page.final_url` | Final resolved URL after redirects. |
| `page.scrape_id` | Opaque scrape identifier for follow-up interactions. |
| `page.title` |  |

+18 more (types in the full schema): `page` {status_code, answer, change_tracking, description, highlights, page_count, source_type, total_page_count}; `page.content` {html, markdown, raw_html, summary}; `page.fetch` {cache_state, cached_at, proxy_tier}; `page.media` {audio_url, screenshot_url, video_url}. Also in the sample: {job_id string} (+13 more).

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/batch-scrape" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"urls":["https://example.com/a","https://example.com/b"]}'
```

## POST /v1/web/crawl - 1-10000 credits (request-shaped)

Starts an async crawl job and returns a SocialCrawl job id (job_...). Poll or cancel it via GET/DELETE /v1/web/jobs/{job_id}, or track it with a webhook.

**Use when** you need many pages from one site; check progress with GET jobs/{job_id}.
**Cost** price depends on how many items the request sends or returns · not cached
**Pricing** 1 credit per page crawled. Submitting holds `limit` credits up front (default limit 10, max 10,000) and the unused portion is refunded when the job settles.
**Execution** Async job: pass `webhook_url` to be told when it completes instead of polling.
**Paging** none

**Body params** (JSON)

- `url` (required) - Root URL to crawl. · e.g. `https://example.com`
- `limit` (optional, integer) - Maximum pages to crawl. · e.g. `10`
- `max_depth` (optional, integer) - How many link hops from the root URL to follow. 1 is the root page and the pages it links to. Leave unset to let `limit` alone bound the crawl.
- `allow_backward_links` (optional, boolean) - Crawl the whole domain rather than only URLs under the starting path. Send it when the root URL is a deep page but you want the entire site.
- `allow_external_links` (optional, boolean) - Follow links off the domain. Off by default, and easy to make expensive: `limit` is the only thing bounding it.
- `include_paths` (optional, string) - CSV of URL path patterns to crawl, e.g. '/blog/.*,/docs/.*'. Everything else is skipped, which is the cheapest way to narrow a crawl.
- `exclude_paths` (optional, string) - CSV of URL path patterns to skip, e.g. '/tag/.*'. Applied after include_paths.
- `webhook_url` (optional, string) - Optional webhook URL for terminal job updates.
- `formats` (optional, string) - CSV of output formats for each crawled page, e.g. 'markdown' (default) or 'markdown,html'.
- `goal` (optional, string) - Optional. What you are looking for on the site, in your own words. SocialCrawl maps the site, scrapes the URLs that likely hold it (always at least two), and lists every skipped URL with p. Without this param the crawl follows links by depth only.

**Response** `Analytics` async job: this call returns `job_id`; poll `GET /v1/web/jobs/{job_id}` for status, and the result comes back there once it completes ([full schema](schemas/Analytics.md)).

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `page.url` | Requested URL. |
| `page.extraction` | Structured extraction result when requested. |
| `page.fetched_at` | Fetch timestamp when reported. |
| `page.final_url` | Final resolved URL after redirects. |
| `page.scrape_id` | Opaque scrape identifier for follow-up interactions. |
| `page.title` |  |

+17 more (types in the full schema): `page` {status_code, answer, change_tracking, description, highlights, page_count, total_page_count}; `page.content` {html, markdown, raw_html, summary}; `page.fetch` {cache_state, cached_at, proxy_tier}; `page.media` {audio_url, screenshot_url, video_url}. Also in the sample: {job_id string, kind string} (+12 more).

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/crawl" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \

```

## GET /v1/web/extract - 5 credits (custom)

Fetches one web page and returns structured extraction output under the WebPage extraction field.

**Use when** you want specific values such as price or author rather than the page's full text.
**Cost** not cached
**Pricing** A flat 5 credits. It runs through the metered pricer for consistency with the rest of the web surface, but nothing in your query changes the charge.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Public URL to extract from. · e.g. `https://example.com/pricing`
- `schema` (optional, string) - JSON object schema describing the data to return.
- `prompt` (optional, string) - Plain-language extraction instruction. · e.g. `Extract plan names and prices.`
- `only_main_content` (optional, boolean) - Strip nav, headers, footers and sidebars and keep the article body. Default true; send false when you need the whole page, including the chrome.
- `timeout` (optional, integer) - Hard cap on each page load in milliseconds, 1 to 30000. A page that exceeds it fails and is refunded rather than returning a partial capture.
- `max_age` (optional, integer) - Accept an upstream-cached copy up to this many milliseconds old, which is faster and costs the same. Default 172800000 (48 hours); send 0 to force a live fetch.
- `proxy` (optional, enum: basic | auto | enhanced) - Proxy tier: basic, auto, or enhanced. Raise it only when a site blocks the default tier - enhanced is slower.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `schema`, `prompt`.

**Response** `WebPage` object at `data`, `{ page }` ([full schema](schemas/WebPage.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `page.url` | Requested URL. |
| `page.extraction` | Structured extraction result when requested. |
| `page.fetched_at` | Fetch timestamp when reported. |
| `page.final_url` | Final resolved URL after redirects. |
| `page.scrape_id` | Opaque scrape identifier for follow-up interactions. |
| `page.status_code` | HTTP status code observed while fetching the page. |

+15 more (types in the full schema): `page.content` {html, markdown, raw_html, summary}; `page.fetch` {cache_state, cached_at, proxy_tier}; `page.media` {audio_url, screenshot_url, video_url}; `page` {answer, change_tracking, highlights, page_count, total_page_count}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/extract" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://example.com/pricing" \
  --data-urlencode "prompt=Extract plan names and prices." \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

Returns the current status, billing settlement, progress, and any available result metadata for one async web job: crawl, batch scrape, or agent. Append /errors to the same path to list per-page failures and robots-blocked URLs (crawl and batch scrape jobs).

**Use when** you want to poll a crawl, batch scrape, or agent job after starting it; add /errors to the path to list failed pages.

**Execution** Job-management route for the async submitters (`web/crawl`, `web/batch-scrape`, `web/agent`). Free to call.

**Path params**

- `job_id` (required) - Job id (job_...) returned by POST /v1/web/crawl, POST /v1/web/batch-scrape, or POST /v1/web/agent as data.job_id. · e.g. `job_9f3k2n8d1`

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/jobs/job_9f3k2n8d1" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## DELETE /v1/web/jobs/{job_id} - free (0 credits)

Cancels one async web job of any kind (crawl, batch scrape, or agent), closes the upstream work when possible, and refunds any unsettled held credits.

**Use when** you want to stop a job you no longer need before it finishes and bills for more pages.
**Cost** not cached
**Execution** Job-management route for the async submitters (`web/crawl`, `web/batch-scrape`, `web/agent`). Free to call.
**Paging** none

**Path params**

- `job_id` (required) - Job id (job_...) returned by POST /v1/web/crawl, POST /v1/web/batch-scrape, or POST /v1/web/agent as data.job_id. · e.g. `job_9f3k2n8d1`

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): {job_id string, kind string, resource string, status string, invalid_urls null, result_ref null, result null, error null, credits_hold number, credits_charged number, created_at string, updated_at string, expires_at string}; `progress` {completed number, total number}.

```bash
curl -X DELETE "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/jobs/job_9f3k2n8d1" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/web/map - 1 credit (custom)

Discovers URLs for a public site and returns them as a normalized WebPageList.

**Use when** you want to discover what pages a site has before choosing which ones to scrape or crawl.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** single page - Fixed-window feed: upstream returns a single non-cursored result set.

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Site URL to map. · e.g. `https://example.com`
- `search` (optional, string) - Optional path or keyword filter.
- `limit` (optional, integer) - Maximum URLs to return, up to 5000. · e.g. `100`
- `sitemap` (optional, enum: include | skip | only) - How to use the site's sitemap.xml: 'include' (default) to merge it with crawled links, 'only' to trust it alone, 'skip' to ignore it.
- `include_subdomains` (optional, boolean) - Follow links onto subdomains of the root URL. Default true.
- `ignore_query_parameters` (optional, boolean) - Treat URLs differing only by query string as one URL, which keeps paginated and tracking-tagged duplicates out of the result. Default true.
- `fresh` (optional, boolean) - Bypass the upstream cache and re-discover the site now. Slower; use it when the map is known to be stale.
- `goal` (optional, string) - Optional. What you are looking for on the site, in your own words. The map still returns every URL, ranked, with skipped_urls listing the ones that look unlikely to hold it (each with p). Without this param the map is unchanged.

**Response** `WebPageList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ page }` ([full schema](schemas/WebPageList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `page.url` | Requested URL. |
| `page.extraction` | Structured extraction result when requested. |
| `page.fetched_at` | Fetch timestamp when reported. |
| `page.final_url` | Final resolved URL after redirects. |
| `page.scrape_id` | Opaque scrape identifier for follow-up interactions. |
| `page.title` |  |

+17 more (types in the full schema): `page` {status_code, answer, change_tracking, description, highlights, page_count, total_page_count}; `page.content` {html, markdown, raw_html, summary}; `page.fetch` {cache_state, cached_at, proxy_tier}; `page.media` {audio_url, screenshot_url, video_url}. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.judged_urls`, `data.skipped_urls`.

**Next** `web/scrape` (`url` ← `data.items[].page.url`) - The full content of each page.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/map" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://example.com" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## POST /v1/web/monitors - free (0 credits)

Creates an upstream-backed monitor. Creation is free; every scheduled check bills its upstream cost plus 1 credit for orchestration, and keeps billing on the cadence you set until the monitor is paused or deleted. The response returns credits_booked, the upstream cost of a single check, so budget (credits_booked + 1) x checks per month before leaving one running.

**Use when** you want to track something for changes over time; for a single look right now, scrape the page instead.
**Cost** not cached
**Pricing** 0 credits to create. Each scheduled check then bills its upstream cost plus 1 credit for orchestration, repeating on `cadence_minutes` until you pause or delete the monitor (a 5-minute cadence is 288 checks a day).
**Execution** Stateful monitor-management route. Managing a monitor is free; each scheduled check bills its own upstream cost plus 1 credit for orchestration.
**Paging** none

**Body params** (JSON)

- `url` (required) - URL or root target to monitor. · e.g. `https://example.com`
- `name` (optional, string) - Human-readable monitor name. · e.g. `Example monitor`
- `mode` (optional, enum: scrape | search) - Monitor target type. · e.g. `scrape`
- `cadence_minutes` (optional, integer) - Check interval in minutes: 5-60, or a whole number of hours up to 1440 (120, 180, ...). Hour cadences are scheduled as cron. · e.g. `15`
- `schedule_text` (optional, string) - Plain-language schedule, such as every 15 minutes.
- `schedule_cron` (optional, string) - Cron schedule. Mutually exclusive with schedule_text.
- `timezone` (optional, string) - IANA timezone for the schedule.
- `webhook_url` (optional, string) - HTTPS URL that receives a signed callback on every check, so you do not have to poll the checks list.
- `query` (optional, string) - Search query the monitor re-runs, used only when mode=search. On a scrape monitor the url is the target instead.
- `goal` (optional, string) - Plain-language description of what a meaningful change looks like, used by the judge to decide whether a check is worth notifying about. A search monitor needs this unless judge_enabled is false.
- `retention_days` (optional, integer) - How long to keep each check's captured result, 1 to 365 days. Older checks are dropped.
- `judge_enabled` (optional, boolean) - Run the LLM judge over each check so you are notified on meaningful changes rather than every byte-level diff. Defaults on, except on a search monitor with no goal.

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): {monitor_id string, url string, mode string, status string, cadence_minutes number, credits_booked number, consecutive_failures number, last_check_at null, next_check_at string, created_at string, updated_at string}; `params` {url string, name string}.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/monitors" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com"}'
```

## GET /v1/web/monitors/{monitor_id} - free (0 credits)

Returns configuration, cadence, status, and billing metadata for one web monitor.

## GET /v1/web/scrape - 1-5 credits (request-shaped)

Fetches a public web page and returns clean content, metadata, and optional media in the unified WebPage schema.

**Use when** you want it for a single known URL; for whole sites start a crawl job instead.
**Cost** price moves with `pdf_parse`, `proxy` · not cached · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 1 credit for a standard scrape. It rises to a flat 5 when the fetch needs more than a plain request: `proxy=auto`, `proxy=enhanced`, or `pdf_parse=true`. Nothing else moves the price, so screenshots, tag filters, `wait_for` and a mobile viewport are all included in the 1 credit.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Public URL to fetch. · e.g. `https://example.com`
- `formats` (optional, string) - Comma-separated output formats such as markdown,screenshot. · e.g. `markdown`
- `only_main_content` (optional, boolean) - Strip nav, headers, footers and sidebars and keep the article body. Default true; send false when you need the whole page, including the chrome. A markdown-only scrape of a site the primary scraper cannot fetch is served by a second extractor, which returns the whole page.
- `wait_for` (optional, integer) - Milliseconds to wait after load before capturing, for pages that render their content in JavaScript. Leave unset unless the page comes back empty or half-built.
- `mobile` (optional, boolean) - Render in a mobile viewport with a mobile user agent. Use it when the site serves a different layout to phones.
- `timeout` (optional, integer) - Hard cap on the page load in milliseconds, 1 to 30000. A page that exceeds it fails and is refunded rather than returning a partial capture.
- `max_age` (optional, integer) - Accept an upstream-cached copy up to this many milliseconds old, which is faster and still one credit. Default 172800000 (48 hours); send 0 to force a live fetch.
- `location_country` (optional, string) - ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code to fetch from, e.g. 'us' or 'de'. Use it for geo-varying pages such as pricing or availability.
- `screenshot_full_page` (optional, boolean) - When a screenshot format is requested, capture the entire scrollable page instead of the visible viewport.
- `include_tags` (optional, string) - CSV of CSS selectors or HTML tags to keep, e.g. 'article,main'. Everything outside them is dropped. Use it to pin extraction to a known container.
- `exclude_tags` (optional, string) - CSV of CSS selectors or HTML tags to drop, e.g. 'nav,footer,.cookie-banner'. Applied after include_tags.
- `proxy` (optional, enum: basic | auto | enhanced) - Proxy tier: basic, auto, or enhanced.
- `pdf_parse` (optional, boolean) - Parse the target as a PDF and return its extracted text. Send it when the URL points at a PDF rather than an HTML page.
- `block_ads` (optional, boolean) - Block ad and tracker requests, which is faster and quieter. Default true.
- `remove_base64_images` (optional, boolean) - Drop inline base64-encoded images from the returned content instead of carrying them in the payload. Default true.

**Response** `WebPage` object at `data`, `{ page }` ([full schema](schemas/WebPage.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `page.url` | Requested URL. |
| `page.extraction` | Structured extraction result when requested. |
| `page.fetched_at` | Fetch timestamp when reported. |
| `page.final_url` | Final resolved URL after redirects. |
| `page.scrape_id` | Opaque scrape identifier for follow-up interactions. |
| `page.status_code` | HTTP status code observed while fetching the page. |

+15 more (types in the full schema): `page.content` {html, markdown, raw_html, summary}; `page.fetch` {cache_state, cached_at, proxy_tier}; `page.media` {audio_url, screenshot_url, video_url}; `page` {answer, change_tracking, highlights, page_count, total_page_count}. Also in the sample: `page.page_state` {value string, confidence number, skipped_judge boolean}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/scrape" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://example.com" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/web/search - 2-120 credits (request-shaped)

Searches web, news, and image sources and returns a single normalized list of web page results.

**Use when** you do not know yet which URLs you need; once you have a URL, scrape it.
**Cost** price moves with `include_content` · cache 120 s
**Pricing** 2 credits per 10 results, so `limit` up to 10 costs 2, 11-20 costs 4, and the 100 maximum costs 20. `include_content=true` adds 1 credit per result, because it scrapes each result page as well as reading the SERP row - that is what takes a 100-result content search to the 120-credit ceiling. The hold settles down to the work actually done.
**Paging** single page - Fixed-window feed: upstream returns a single non-cursored result set.

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Search query. · e.g. `social media data api`
- `sources` (optional, string) - Comma-separated sources: web,news,images.
- `categories` (optional, string) - CSV of source categories to restrict the search to, e.g. 'github,research'. Omit for an unrestricted web search.
- `limit` (optional, integer) - Results per source, from 1 to 100. · e.g. `10`
- `country` (optional, string) - ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code the search is run from, e.g. 'US' (default) or 'GB'. Changes which results rank.
- `location` (optional, string) - Free-text locality to bias results towards, e.g. 'London, United Kingdom'. Finer-grained than country.
- `time_range` (optional, string) - Recency window as a Google `tbs` value: 'qdr:d' past day, 'qdr:w' past week, 'qdr:m' past month, 'qdr:y' past year.
- `sort_by_date` (optional, boolean) - Sort newest-first instead of by relevance. Combines with time_range rather than replacing it.
- `include_domains` (optional, string) - CSV of domains to restrict results to, e.g. 'nytimes.com,ft.com'. Cannot be combined with exclude_domains - sending both is a 400 before billing.
- `exclude_domains` (optional, string) - CSV of domains to drop from the results. Cannot be combined with include_domains.
- `include_content` (optional, boolean) - Also scrape each result and return its page content as markdown, not just the SERP row. This is what makes the call expensive: it scrapes one page per result, which is why the range runs to 120 credits.

**Response** `WebPageList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ page }` ([full schema](schemas/WebPageList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `page.url` | Requested URL. |
| `page.extraction` | Structured extraction result when requested. |
| `page.fetched_at` | Fetch timestamp when reported. |
| `page.final_url` | Final resolved URL after redirects. |
| `page.scrape_id` | Opaque scrape identifier for follow-up interactions. |
| `page.title` |  |

+18 more (types in the full schema): `page` {status_code, answer, change_tracking, description, highlights, page_count, source_type, total_page_count}; `page.content` {html, markdown, raw_html, summary}; `page.fetch` {cache_state, cached_at, proxy_tier}; `page.media` {audio_url, screenshot_url, video_url}. Page-level: `data.dropped`.

**Next** `web/scrape` (`url` ← `data.items[].page.url`) - The full content of each page.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/search" \
  --data-urlencode "query=social media data api" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## POST /v1/web/sessions - 5-20 credits (request-shaped)

Creates a short-lived browser session for follow-up interactions.

**Use when** a page needs clicking, typing, or logging in before the content you want appears.
**Cost** not cached
**Pricing** 20 credits per browser-hour, minimum 5. The hold is taken from `ttl_seconds` when the session is created (60s default = 5, the 3,600s maximum = 20) and settled when it closes.
**Execution** Stateful browser-session route. The session itself is billed by duration when it is created; managing and closing it is free.
**Paging** single page - Fixed-window feed: upstream returns a single non-cursored result set.

**Body params** (JSON)

- `url` (required) - URL to open in the session after creation. · e.g. `https://example.com`
- `ttl_seconds` (optional, integer) - Session TTL in seconds. · e.g. `60`
- `activity_ttl_seconds` (optional, integer) - Idle timeout in seconds: the session closes this long after the last interaction, even if ttl_seconds has not elapsed. Closing early settles the hold down, so it lowers the bill.
- `stream_web_view` (optional, boolean) - Return a live view URL in the response so a human can watch the session drive the page.

**Response** `WebPage` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): {session_id string, kind string, status string, ttl_seconds number, credits_hold number, credits_billed number, expires_at string, closed_at null, created_at string, updated_at string}.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/sessions" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com"}'
```

## POST /v1/web/sessions/{session_id}/execute - free (0 credits)

Runs code in an existing browser session and returns the execution result.

**Use when** you want to drive a live page through the Playwright page, browser and chromium globals. With node the value lands in result; bash and python print to stdout.
**Cost** not cached
**Paging** none

**Path params**

- `session_id` (required) - SocialCrawl session id. · e.g. `ws_3g7x1v5m2`

**Body params** (JSON)

- `code` (required) - Code to execute in the browser sandbox. · e.g. `await page.goto("https://example.com"); console.log(await page.title());`
- `language` (optional, enum: node | python | bash) - Execution language: node, python, or bash. · e.g. `node`
- `timeout` (optional, integer) - Execution timeout in seconds, from 1 to 40 (default 30). Larger values are capped at 40 so the call always returns inside the request window; a script still running at the cap returns a 504 UPSTREAM_ERROR envelope. Split longer work across several calls to the same session.

**Response** `WebPage` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): {success boolean, stdout string, stderr string, result null, exitCode number, killed boolean}.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/web/sessions/ws_3g7x1v5m2/execute" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"code":"await page.goto(\"https://example.com\"); console.log(await page.title());"}'
```
